Introduction
This document provides essential information on the components of the Carbon Emissions Key Issue to
enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI S&C’s) outputs
are determined. Carbon Emissions is a Key Issue in the Environmental Pillar of the MSCI ESG Ratings
model. Companies are evaluated on the carbon intensity of their operations and their efforts to manage
climate-related risks and opportunities.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of
“ESG Ratings Methodology.”

Carbon Emissions Mitigation score
The Carbon Emissions Mitigation score evaluates the company’s ability to manage and reduce carbon
emissions through mitigation measures, including energy efficiency, cleaner energy use, carbon capture,
demand-side management and other reduction efforts. Highest performance reflects aggressive,
comprehensive programs across operations and value chain. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10
indicates strong initiatives.
• Use of cleaner sources of energy.
Definition: Assesses how aggressively the company has sought to mitigate its carbon emissions through
the use of cleaner sources of energy such as solar, wind, geothermal, co-generation, or natural gas in
place of oil or coal.
• Efforts to capture GHG emissions.
Definition: Assesses the aggressiveness of a company’s efforts to use greenhouse gas (GHG) capture
and storage/sequestration of its operational emissions.

• Energy Consumption Management & Operational Efficiency
Definition: This data point indicates our assessment of how aggressively the company has sought to
mitigate its carbon emissions by managing energy consumption and improving the energy efficiency of
its operations. Possible values are: 'Aggressive efforts' (best); 'Some efforts'; 'Limited
efforts/information'; 'No efforts' (worst)
• Efforts to reduce customer energy consumption (demand-side management)
Definition: Indicates MSCI ESG Research's assessment of the aggressiveness of a company's efforts to
reduce future energy consumption through energy efficiency or demand response programs. This
indicator is specifically relevant for energy companies and utilities.
• Other efforts to reduce carbon emissions.
Definition: Assesses how aggressively the company has sought to mitigate its operational and/or value
chain carbon emissions through other efforts (including purchasing carbon offsets, but excluding energy
efficiency, clean energy use, carbon capture or demand-side management). The assessment is based
on industry-specific criteria.
Carbon Emissions Targets score
The Carbon Emissions Targets score evaluates the company’s initiatives to set, pursue, and verify
carbon emissions targets. Highest initiatives reflect comprehensive, independently verified targets with
strong progress toward achievement. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong
initiatives.
• Carbon emissions target comprehensiveness
Definition: Assesses the extent to which the company has established quantitative climate targets that
are comprehensive in scope and complete in coverage. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating
comprehensive targets.
 Carbon emissions target footprint coverage (%)
Definition: Assesses the extent to which the company’s emission reduction targets cover its
total reported emissions. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates that the targets
comprehensively cover all relevant emissions.
 Carbon emissions target relevant scope score
Definition: Assesses whether the company’s emission reduction targets include all financially
material scopes. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates full coverage of financially
material emission scopes.

• Carbon emissions target progress
Definition: Assesses the company’s progress toward active environmental targets, as well as its
historical track record in meeting previously stated targets. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating
strong progress towards targets
 Carbon emissions ongoing target progress
Definition: Assesses the company’s progress toward achieving its emission reduction targets
based on current performance. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 all its targets are on
track to meet stated targets.
 Carbon emissions target track record
Definition: Assesses the company’s historical performance in achieving or maintaining
sustainability or environmental targets. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong
performance.
• Carbon emissions target verification
Definition: Assesses whether the company’s disclosed targets are supported by the Science Based
Targets initiative (SBTi), where applicable. Expressed as either NULL or 10 score, with 10 indicating
presence of verification.
 SBTi long-term target status
Definition: Indicates the status of the company’s Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi)
long-term target, aligned with net-zero or long-term decarbonization goals.
 SBTi near-term target status
Definition: Indicates the status of the company’s Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi)
near-term target, aligned with short- to medium-term emissions reduction goals.
Carbon Emissions Performance score
The Carbon Emissions Performance score evaluates the company's performance on carbon emissions
metrics (including greenhouse gas emissions intensity), relative to its peers. It is expressed as a 0–10
score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
• Carbon emissions performance relative to peers.
Definition: Assesses the company's performance on greenhouse gas [GHG] emissions intensity
(normalized by sales or by units of production), and trend in GHG emissions intensity, relative to its
peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
o Carbon emissions intensity industry relative score
Definition: Assesses the company's performance on greenhouse gas [GHG] emissions intensity
(normalized by sales or by units of production), relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score,
where 10 indicates strong performance.

 Three-year average carbon emissions intensity (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average greenhouse-gas emissions
per unit of sales over the defined period.
 Three-year average carbon emissions intensity (production based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average greenhouse-gas emissions
per unit production (megawatt-hour generated, or ton cement produced or revenue
passenger kilometer, based on industry).
o Carbon emissions intensity industry relative trend score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of year-over-year
carbon-emissions intensity trend (normalized by sales or by units of production), relative to its
peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average year-over-year carbon emissions intensity trend (sales
based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year
greenhouse-gas emissions (per unit of sales) trend.
 Three-year average year-over-year carbon emissions intensity trend (production
based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average year-over-year greenhouse-
gas emissions per unit production (megawatt-hour generated, or ton cement
produced or revenue passenger kilometer based on industry) trend.
Sources: Company disclosures, CDP

Business Segment Exposure scores
The Business Segment Exposure score of a business segment is based on a mapping of the business
segment as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity. MSCI S&C uses the
Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific adjustments to define
business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to calculate a Business
Segment Exposure score. Each business activity score is determined by aggregating normalized Scope 1
and Scope 2 GHG emissions intensities to a business activity level.

The Emissions Intensity score indicates the baseline risk faced by a business segment. For each SIC
code, this score is calculated by considering the reported company level scopes 1 and 2 emissions.
To calculate the score:
1. For each SIC code, the median emissions intensity is computed using data from companies that
have majority of their assets value from activities mapped to that SIC code.
o Emissions intensity is expressed as metric tons of CO equivalent (mtCO e) per million
USD in sales.

2. If no company derives more than 50% of its revenue from the activities mapped to a specific SIC
code, the calculation defaults to the next broader level in the SIC code hierarchy.
3. The resulting emissions intensity per business segment is then log-transformed and scaled to a
0–10 range, where higher scores indicate greater emissions intensity and baseline carbon
emissions exposure.
For business activities related to electricity transmission and distribution (T&D) and power generation,
the Business Segment Exposure score is derived by aggregating the emissions intensities of pure-play
T&D companies as assessed by MSCI.

The near-term ambition of a country is assessed by considering the annual emissions reduction rate
needed to meet their publicly disclosed near-term climate targets. Countries or markets with aggressive
near-term targets have high emissions reduction rates and therefore a higher policy pressure segment
score.

A country or market’s long-term ambition indicates the strength and credibility of its long-term climate
targets such as net-zero commitments. Long term targets could signal the direction of future policy and
regulatory developments, even in the near term.
The government and market mechanisms score indicates the current strength of policy and market-
based mechanisms signaling a government’s commitment to driving the energy transition.
This score is calculated as the average of carbon pricing score and fossil fuel subsidies score.

• 𝐶𝐶𝐸𝐸𝑀𝑀 is the Fossil Fuel Subsidies score.
𝐹𝐹𝐹𝐹𝑆𝑆
Carbon pricing mechanisms score indicates mechanisms such as carbon taxes or emissions trading
systems that exert policy pressure on companies by assigning a direct cost to carbon emissions.
The fossil fuel subsidies score indicates the degree of financial support for fossil fuel consumption.
Lower subsidies (higher scores) increase transition pressure by removing cost advantages, whereas high
subsidies (lower scores) signal continued alignment with fossil fuel-based economic structures, thus
reducing policy pressure
In the absence of evidence from data sources indicating that a country has near- or long-term emissions
reduction targets or carbon pricing mechanisms in place, a score of 0 is assigned. In the absence of a
country’s fossil fuel subsidy information, a score of 5 is assigned.
